title: Impact of Annealing and Strain on Magnetic and Magnetocaloric Properties of FeNiMnSiGe High-Entropy Alloy Nanoribbons Prepared by Magnetron Co-Sputtering.

recollection.starting_material: FeNiMnSiGe thin ribbons deposited by magnetron co-sputtering (a multicomponent high-entropy alloy film)
recollection.intervention: Post-deposition annealing at various temperatures and application of controlled uniaxial bending/ tensile strain
recollection.structure: Crystalline BCC/B2-like nano-grained ribbons whose grain size and lattice parameter change with heat treatment and strain
recollection.mechanism: Annealing promotes chemical short-range ordering and grain growth, while external strain modifies lattice spacing; both effects tune magnetic exchange interactions among Fe, Ni and Mn atoms, altering the first-order magneto-structural transition that governs the magnetocaloric response
recollection.results: Guess: optimal annealing (~600 °C, 1 h) raises the Curie temperature from ~260 K to ~300 K and increases the isothermal magnetic entropy change |ΔS_M| to ~6 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ under 2 T; additional 1 % tensile strain further enhances |ΔS_M| to ~7 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and broadens the working temperature span to ~60 K

score.note: The recollection generically identifies annealing and tensile strain, as already indicated by the title, but misses the specific 700 K treatment, strain ranges, and ribbon spacing comparison. It incorrectly describes a crystalline nanograined BCC/B2 structure, grain growth, and a first-order magnetostructural transition; the material remained amorphous/disordered without detectable recrystallization. The recalled temperatures, entropy changes, field, and strain effects are far from the reported values.
